newsitem.title: USA: Amoco says natgas Gulf output mostly restored.
newsitem.headline: Amoco says natgas Gulf output mostly restored.

text.p: Amoco Corp said Monday it had restored about 90 percent of natural gas output shut-in as a precautionary measure in the U.S. Gulf due to a storm. About 60 percent of gross production was shut as Tropical Storm Josephine approached the Gulf Coast on Sunday.

"Some gas was shut in. We have an automatic system that shuts (output) depending on the pressure," John Curry, public affairs advisor for Amoco said, adding the remaining 10 percent of shut capacity should be restored by noon Tuesday.
Amoco's daily output in the U.S. Gulf is some 609 million cubic feet a day (mmcfd).
The company's crude oil production in the U.S. Gulf, meanwhile, was not interrupted by the storm.
Curry said Amoco had started to evacuate employees from offshore oil platforms and drilling rigs since Friday.
But some personnel from the western part of the Gulf returned to work today.
